sections.title: Habitats
lines: Fresh water (summoning appendix)

sections.title: Appearance
lines: An elongated fish. The portrait uses a rounded body and blunt head based on freshwater electric eels. The printed combat entry gives no color or size.

sections.title: Damage immunities
lines: Electricity

sections.title: Combat mechanics
lines: Electrical discharge · The discharge reaches 15 feet. A target under 5 feet away takes 3d8, one 5 to 10 feet away takes 2d8, and one farther out within range takes 1d8. The eel recharges for an hour between discharges.
Electrical immunity · Electrical effects do not harm this eel.

sections.title: Table notes
lines: 1–3 appearing. Unsteady (7) morale.
The ordinary Electric Eel appears in Fresh Water Monster Summoning II on p. 378. The Fish paragraph gives no further habitat detail.
Monstrous Manual, TSR 2140, January 1994 third printing, Fish pp. 117–118 and aquatic summoning p. 378.

sections.title: Habitats
lines: Aquatic habitat, salinity unspecified

sections.title: Appearance
lines: A large, long-bodied eel with teeth. The portrait gives it a broad head and toothy jaws. The printed entry gives no measured length or coloration.

sections.title: Combat mechanics
lines: Fast bite · It attacks with its teeth for 3–18 damage and gets +1 to initiative rolls. The Fish prose explicitly says it has no electrical discharge.

sections.title: Table notes
lines: 1–4 appearing. Average (8) morale.
The Fresh Water summoning table on p. 378 separately names an eel called “giant electric.” The entry gives no basis to use that name for this non-electric Giant Eel.
Monstrous Manual, TSR 2140, January 1994 third printing, Fish pp. 117–118 and aquatic summoning p. 378.

sections.title: Habitats
lines: Salt water (summoning appendix)
Fresh water (summoning appendix)

sections.title: Appearance
lines: A long-bodied eel. The portrait uses a narrow moray-like head and mottled blue-gray skin. The book gives no measured length or coloration.

sections.title: Damage immunities
lines: Electricity

sections.title: Hit Dice variants mechanics
lines: 6 HD · THAC0 13, table damage 2–8, 420 XP.
7 HD · THAC0 13, table damage 3–12, 650 XP.
8 HD · THAC0 12, table damage 4–16, 975 XP.

sections.title: Combat mechanics
lines: Electrical discharge · The discharge reaches 15 feet. A target under 5 feet away takes 6d6, one 5 to 10 feet away takes 4d6, and one farther out within range takes 2d6. A failed save vs. paralyzation stuns the victim for a number of rounds equal to the damage received. The Marine Eel entry gives no recharge interval.
Electrical immunity · Electrical effects do not harm this eel.

sections.title: Table notes
lines: 1 appearing. Average (9) morale.
Both Salt Water and Fresh Water Monster Summoning VI list the Marine Eel. The numeric damage in its table row is separate from the discharge dice in its description.
Monstrous Manual, TSR 2140, January 1994 third printing, Fish pp. 117–118 and aquatic summoning p. 378.

sections.title: Habitats
lines: Fresh and salt water, 25 to 40 feet deep
Colony caves and connected tunnels

sections.title: Appearance
lines: A slender eel with a long tapering body in the portrait. The printed entry describes its narrow lair holes but gives no measured body length or color.

sections.title: Combat mechanics
lines: Poison bite · The bite deals 1 damage. A victim who fails a save vs. poison dies in 1d4 rounds under the printed game rule.

sections.title: Lair mechanics
lines: Colony tunnels · A central cave about 30 feet long and 20 feet wide and high connects to 6-foot-diameter tunnels and individual homes 6 to 8 inches across. The colony guards its young in the central cave.
Scavenged objects · The cave floor holds small stones, coins, and gems brought back by the eels.

sections.title: Table notes
lines: 10–60 appearing. Unsteady (6) morale.
The table prints 1−1 Hit Dice.
Monstrous Manual, TSR 2140, January 1994 third printing, Fish pp. 117–118 and aquatic summoning p. 378.
